taskTitle: Where ten HTTP header fields are defined

checks.detail: 0 state changes, each allowed by a review (0 reviews in all)
1 phase had the tools designed for them

finalText:
All ten fields are defined in RFCs I opened and read. I did not find any sign that these RFCs have been obsoleted. That check was limited: the pages I opened showed no "Obsoleted by" notice, and one search turned up no replacement RFC. RFC 9110 and RFC 9111 are the HTTP specs that replaced RFC 7230–7235 and the older HTTP/1.1 specs, and RFC 8288 itself obsoletes RFC 5988.

- **Age, Cache-Control, Expires:** RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching), sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3.
- **Last-Modified, ETag, Location, Retry-After, Vary:** RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics), sections 8.8.2, 8.8.3, 10.2.2, 10.2.3 and 12.5.5.
- **Strict-Transport-Security:** RFC 6797, section 6.1.
- **Link:** RFC 8288, section 3.

Sources: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html
